questions.q: Label each madd in «فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ» (79:34).
questions.a: فَإِذَا: natural (2); جَآءَتِ: muttasil (4 or 5); ٱلطَّآمَّةُ: lazim (6); ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ: natural (2), even at the stop, because the word ends on the madd letter.

questions.q: A madd with no cause is ...
Sort (pupil PDF): put ten madds from 79:1 to 20 into natural, muttasil or munfasil, with the counts. Today's rota group recites 'Abasa to the teacher.
questions.a: For example: ٱلنَّٰزِعَٰتِ natural; مُوسَىٰٓ munfasil when joined to إِذْ (79:16), natural at a stop; إِلَىٰٓ أَن munfasil; ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ natural.

questions.q: Extend: explain why 'arid lis-sukun only happens when stopping.
questions.a: The sukoon is not fixed: it appears only because we stop on the word.

questions.q: Stretch: give one madd of each family from Al-Fatihah.
questions.a: Natural: مَٰلِكِ; 'arid: ٱلرَّحِيمِ at the stop; lazim: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ.
A) Muttasil. Alif then hamza in the same word: muttasil, 4 or 5.

questions.q: Think again: Why might Allah's Book be recited with exact lengths, when everyday speech is not so careful?
questions.a: It is Allah's word, recited exactly as the Prophet ﷺ taught it; exact lengths keep it unchanged.
